summary: B4 covers promoting 'HITL patch application' (builder-hitl apply-patch) and 'rollback execution' (builder-hitl rollback) from MERGED_BUT_NOT_OPERATIONAL to OPERATIONALLY_VERIFIED. The executors are fully merged and real: apply_hitl_patch performs digest-checked git apply on a clean repo, auto-generates a digest-bound reverse-patch rollback plan, postflight, receipt, and rollback bundle; rollback_hitl_patch executes git apply -R with digest binding and emits an EXECUTED rollback receipt. The CORE demo loop already exercises the entire propose→approve→apply→verify→rollback→postflight→chain-verify lifecycle end-to-end against a detached AssetOverflow/core worktree and is itself OPERATIONALLY_VERIFIED (DEMO_ONLY_VERIFIED assurance). What blocks B4 is not the mutation mechanics but the governance envelope for generic targets: (1) no production patch-approval artifact exists — apply only compares a bare patch_digest field and the generic approval_record kind is hardcoded to Goose command proposals, so the only real approval producer is the demo-scoped core_demo_approval; (2) no promoted way to produce the required pre-apply verification receipt for a generic repo — the B1 bounded runner supports only fixed platform_status/docs_audit profiles and the demo receipt validator requires target.name=="core"; (3) rollback has no distinct human approval (the CLI passes the machine-generated rollback plan path as approval_ref, and command authority only checks non-emptiness); (4) tests mock/monkeypatch the validators, there are zero CLI-level or failure-path tests, and no ledger event is emitted despite the B2 plan requiring one; (5) five docs contradict the merged reality, and matrix states plus pinned test constants (operationally_verified_count==15, BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE assertions) must be flipped together with a receipts-backed live-run audit as promotion evidence.

risks: Weak approval boundary is currently exploitable in principle: any JSON file containing a matching patch_digest authorizes source mutation via apply_hitl_patch (builder_ii/hitl_patch_apply.py line 237), and any non-empty --approval path satisfies command authority (command_authority.py lines 334-336). Promoting without B4.1/B4.3 would certify a nominal, not real, human boundary.

Receipts already self-declare governance.capability_state 'OPERATIONALLY_VERIFIED' and the bundle claims 'MUTATION_WITH_ROLLBACK_VERIFIED' (hitl_patch_apply.py lines 174-189, 314, 383-387, 484-486) while the matrix says MERGED_BUT_NOT_OPERATIONAL — this truth drift could mislead downstream consumers of the artifacts and trips the platform's own artifact-is-authority principle.

Test suite overstates assurance: mocked verification-receipt validation and global VALIDATORS monkeypatching (tests/test_hitl_patch_apply.py, tests/test_hitl_patch_rollback.py) mean the merged E2E path has never been proven with real, schema-valid approval and verification artifacts; the monkeypatched global dict also leaks across the test session (test isolation hazard).

Promotion is a multi-file lockstep change: matrix rows, operationally_verified_count==15, BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE assertions, and five docs must change atomically or docs-truth/platform-truth tests will fail; sequencing B4.8 after B4.7 evidence is mandatory.

Generalizing verification receipts to arbitrary target repos (B4.2) expands the B1 bounded-execution envelope — running checks inside untrusted target repos risks scope creep beyond the fixed shell=False/no-ambient-env envelope the platform deliberately promoted for only two fixed profiles (verification_execution_runner.py); design review needed to avoid quietly promoting arbitrary command execution.

Rollback correctness assumes git apply -R of the recorded forward diff cleanly reverses the applied state; if the operator or another process touches the tree between apply and rollback, rollback fails with no failure receipt and no documented interruption-recovery path (RUNTIME_PROMOTION.md requires 'clear recovery path after interruption').

The core demo lane accepts a core-demo verification receipt only for target.name=='core' but the generic lane requires B1 receipts that cannot target generic repos — until B4.2 lands, any 'live run on a real repo' evidence for B4.7 can only be produced by bending validation, which would invalidate the proof.
